name: Cervical cancer
theme: the preventable disease · the chemoradiation-IO turn

meta.title: Cervical cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with cervical carcinoma - the registry's screening-preventable disease, HPV-driven in essentially all cases (squamous ~90%, adenocarcinoma ~10%, both covered; neuroendocrine cervical carcinoma reroutes to small-cell principles). A young population by oncology's standards, which makes fertility, menopause, and sexual health first-class agenda items rather than footnotes. The surgical chapter teaches a PAIRED LESSON unique in this registry: de-escalating the operation's EXTENT proved safe (SHAPE: simple hysterectomy non-inferior in low-risk disease) while de-escalating its ACCESS ROUTE proved harmful (LACC: minimally invasive radical hysterectomy INFERIOR to open, confirmed at final OS) - less radical yes, less invasive no. The locally-advanced chapter carries the chemoradiation-IO turn (KEYNOTE-A18) with its negative contrast (CALLA) and its honest negative (OUTBACK) - and above everything sits the prevention beat: this disease is vaccine-preventable and screening-preventable, and most deaths occur in the never- and under-screened.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease prevention already knows how to end. Early stage: the PAIRED SURGERY LESSON - SHAPE (verified: simple hysterectomy non-inferior for low-risk disease, with less urologic and sexual morbidity; wrong-PMID catch #26 lives on this citation, where near-identical-title correspondence posed as the primary) beside LACC (verified: minimally invasive radical hysterectomy ran roughly triple the progression hazard of open surgery, stopped early, final OS confirming) - the same era de-escalated extent and re-escalated access, and the trainer teaches why…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: FIGO 2018 staging; HPV-driven biology as the unifying axis; NCCN Cervical v2.2026 (version PMID-matched via JNCCN; content secondhand - 403)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 for advanced disease; the locally-advanced era's load-bearing read is completion of definitive chemoradiation without progression (the consolidation-era entry ticket)

Newly diagnosed.name: Hysterectomy by the paired lesson (SHAPE extent + LACC access)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN early-stage framework (secondhand); SHAPE and LACC both practice-changing
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (SHAPE non-inferiority; LACC superiority-of-open) - the paired lesson verified
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the operation's ledger, deliberately smaller where SHAPE applies - urologic and sexual morbidity are the honest currencies
Newly diagnosed.patient: For early disease: an operation cures most - and two major trials refined it in opposite directions: low-risk tumors need a SMALLER operation than before, but when the bigger operation is needed, it should be done OPEN, not by keyhole.
drugs: Simple or open radical hysterectomy + node assessment

Newly diagnosed.name: Fertility-sparing surgery (conization / trachelectomy - narrow edges, real option)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: PDQ fertility-sparing pathways (live); NCCN specifics secondhand
Newly diagnosed.evidence: observational/series-grade in selected patients (labeled, never ranked)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cervical-insufficiency obstetric care in future pregnancies - the option's honest downstream cost
Newly diagnosed.patient: For small early tumors when children are still wanted: operations that remove the cancer and keep the uterus - real, proven in careful series, with honestly narrow eligibility edges.

Newly diagnosed.name: Cisplatin-chemoradiation + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-A18 - the turn)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved 2024-01 for III-IVA (secondhand-precise); the CRT backbone level-1 since 1999
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (A18 - PFS and OS verified) atop the 1999 backbone; the negatives (CALLA, OUTBACK) and the contested (INTERLACE) all named
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the pelvic chemoradiation season (bowel, bladder, marrow) plus the immune ledger - and brachytherapy's survivorship items taught from day one
Newly diagnosed.patient: For locally advanced disease: the proven radiation-plus-chemotherapy cure attempt, now with immunotherapy added - the first real improvement to this backbone in a generation, raising three-year survival meaningfully.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab (KEYNOTE-826 - the 1L standard)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (KEYNOTE-826 final OS verified; BEATcc verified) - the median figure itself flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemo season + immune ledger + (where bev) the fistula-vigilance note this disease specifically earns
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread disease: chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (sometimes with an antibody added) - proven to extend life, now the standard first move.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; hemostatic radiotherapy and diversion decisions are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - with a team whose craft includes this disease's specific hard problems.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tisotumab vedotin (innovaTV 301 - the ADC with the ocular ledger)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the ocular ledger leads (conjunctival events - drops, cold packs, exams), plus neuropathy and bleeding watches
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: After first-line treatment: a guided-missile drug that beat chemotherapy on survival itself - with eye care built into every cycle as its known cost.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Cemiplimab (EMPOWER-Cervical 1 - the IO-naive door)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS met (verified); the squeeze honesty carried
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For patients whose first treatment did not include immunotherapy: the immune drug alone extends life versus more chemotherapy - a door that stays open only for the not-yet-exposed.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after the proven lines is a real road - and this card carries the honest map note: the biggest hoped-for next trial closed to new patients in May, and a live alternative is named on the trial screen.

SHAPE sexual-health/QoL companion: the morbidity difference made measurable - the survivorship agenda's anchor. (PMID 39353164, pubmed-url-match)

Ramirez et al. LACC: minimally invasive vs open radical hysterectomy - MIS INFERIOR (progression hazard roughly tripled; stopped early at 631/740). NEJM 2018 (PMID 30380365, pubmed-url-match; FINAL OS confirms inferiority - PMID 38810208, matched). The counterintuitive access lesson; ROCC re-asks it properly

The 1999 cisplatin-chemoradiation backbone (Rose/Morris/Keys NEJM trio + NCI alert): concurrent cisplatin-CRT as the locally-advanced standard - the accompanying NEJM editorial PMID-MATCHED (10202172); the trio's individual PMIDs FLAGGED (citations consistent, links never surfaced - not guessed)

Lorusso et al. KEYNOTE-A18/ENGOT-cx11/GOG-3047: pembrolizumab + definitive CRT - 24-mo PFS 68% vs 57% (HR 0.70). Lancet 2024 (PMID 38521086, pubmed-url-match). FDA 2024-01-12 for FIGO III-IVA (fda.gov snippet-verified; PFS HR 0.59 in that subgroup)
KEYNOTE-A18 overall survival: 36-month OS 82.6% vs 74.8% (HR 0.67, CI 0.50-0.90) - the turn's survival receipt. Lancet 2024 (PMID 39288779, pubmed-url-match)
CALLA: durvalumab + CRT - NEGATIVE (same idea as A18, different result - the honest contrast that keeps the turn's win from reading as inevitable). (PMID 38039991, pubmed-url-match)

Mileshkin et al. OUTBACK: adjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel AFTER definitive CRT - NEGATIVE: 5-yr OS 72% vs 71% (HR 0.90, p=0.81), added toxicity and nothing else. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:468-82 - title and results PUBLISHER-VERIFIED; the PMID (37080223) appeared only in AI summaries and NEVER url-matched across 3 queries: FLAGGED, not stamped. The honest negative guarding against adjuvant drift

McCormack et al. INTERLACE: 6 weeks induction carboplatin-paclitaxel before CRT - 5-yr OS 80% vs 72% (HR 0.60), PFS HR 0.65. Lancet 2024 (PMID 39419054, pubmed-url-match). CONTESTED: a live 2025 Lancet correspondence disputes it as a new standard (induction-era vs A18-era populations) - carried as a debated option, not settled SOC

Colombo/Monk et al. KEYNOTE-826: pembrolizumab + chemo +/- bev, 1L persistent/recurrent/metastatic - PFS and OS significantly longer (primary NEJM 2021 PMID 34534429; FINAL OS JCO 2023 PMID 37910822 - both pubmed-url-matched; exact medians not snippet-captured, the card's figure flagged); HRQoL companion PMID 36878237 matched
Oaknin et al. BEATcc: atezolizumab + platinum/paclitaxel/bevacizumab 1L - improved PFS and OS; the concordant second 1L door. Lancet 2024 (PMID 38048793, pubmed-url-match)

Vergote et al. innovaTV 301: tisotumab vedotin (tissue-factor ADC) vs chemo, 2L/3L - median OS 11.5 vs 9.5 (HR 0.70, p=0.004); FULL FDA approval 2024-04-29 (conversion from 2021 accelerated - fda.gov snippet). The ocular ledger is the counseling signature. NEJM 2024 (PMID 38959480, pubmed-url-match)

Tewari et al. EMPOWER-Cervical 1/GOG-3016: cemiplimab vs chemo post-platinum (IO-naive) - median OS 12.0 vs 8.5. NEJM 2022 (PMID 35139273, pubmed-url-match). The squeeze honesty: an IO-naive receipt in an increasingly IO-treated world

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

NRG-GY037 (NCT07061977): induction pembro-chemo -> pembro-CRT -> maintenance vs the A18 standard, high-risk locally advanced, phase 3, PFS primary (n=336, NCI/NRG) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-05/06), registry re-check due

No recruiting US TIL trial at phase 2+ this sweep
